prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer standing high on an indoor staircase looking down into a lower landing (3 to 5 metres away, rendered dark) bordered by a left wall, an overhanging central wall/upper flight on the right, and descending steps in the bottom foreground. In frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, a standing man in a yellow plaid shirt is below and to the left at roughly 2 to 2.5 metres from the wearer, with a vertical metal railing post on the steps about 1.5 metres below and in front of the wearer and within arm's reach of the standing man's left hand. A diagonal metal handrail in the bottom-left of frames 1, 4, and 5 and the overhanging stairwell wall on the right of frames 2, 3, and 5 appear bright white within 0.3 to 0.8 metres (arm's reach of the wearer), while in frame 3 the camera pans right so the overhanging wall and ascending upper stairs at 0.5 to 1.5 metres occlude the standing man. Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns their head right toward the upper stairwell between frames 1 and 3 and back to the left in frames 4 and 5, causing the nearby handrail and standing man to exit the left edge in frame 3 before re-entering and shifting left again in frame 5. The depth map makes the steep vertical drop, step-by-step distance gradient, and close proximity of the overhanging stairwell wall and foreground handrail much clearer than the RGB image alone, but it is unreliable beyond 3 metres where the floor clutter, tools, metal pipes, and a crouching person at the top-center (~4 metres away, ~2.5 metres behind the standing man) vanish into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates very few elements of the stairwell scene on a black background, detecting only the standing man on the left (`person`, ~2 to 2.5 metres below and left of the camera wearer) in frames 1 and 4, and the distant crouching figure (`person`, ~4 metres away in the upper-middle background, ~2.5 metres from the standing man) in frame 1. In frame 1, the standing man faces his body toward the bottom-right stairs while turning his head up to look at the camera wearer, whereas in frame 4 he stands behind the foreground diagonal handrail (which partially occludes his lower legs) and looks forward/right toward the stairs rather than at the wearer. Also in frame 1, a blue-and-yellow flattened cardboard box on the floor ~3 metres below the wearer and ~1.5 metres to the right of the standing man is segmented, and the same box is segmented again in frame 5 as the camera turns right. While the mask silhouettes in frame 1 help separate the distant crouching figure and the standing man's torso contour from the visually cluttered floor in the RGB strip, the map is highly unreliable overall. It completely misses the standing man when he is partially cropped at the left frame edge in frames 2 and 5, misses the crouching person in frames 2 through 5, fails to segment the stairs, walls, railings, pipes, or tools within arm's reach of either person, and misclassifies the floor cardboard box as a `laptop` in frame 1 and a `book` in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body skeletons against a black background for the standing man (~2 to 2.5 metres below and to the left of the camera wearer) in frames 1 and 4, and a small cluster of keypoints on the lower landing (~3.5 metres below and slightly left of center) in frame 2. In frame 1, the skeleton's wide shoulder-to-hip trapezoid and facial keypoints show the man facing his torso toward the stairs to his left while angling his head upward toward the camera wearer, with his left wrist extending down within arm's reach of the lower stair post and floor box and his legs clipped at the knees. After disappearing in frames 2 and 3 as the wearer turns right and the man is cropped out of view on the left, his skeleton reappears in frame 4 with a narrower torso profile and head keypoints oriented up and to the right, showing that he has turned his head away from the camera wearer toward the staircase while his lower legs are occluded behind the foreground handrail. This skeletal geometry makes the change in the standing man's torso twist and head orientation between frames 1 and 4 easier to read than in the high-angle RGB view alone. However, the map is unreliable across the rest of the sequence: it completely misses the standing man when his head is cropped out at the left border in frames 2 and 5, fails to detect the distant crouching person ~4 metres away in all frames (apart from spurious keypoints near floor clutter in frame 2), and detects no magenta hand skeletons or camera-wearer limbs anywhere.
